top_story: US strikes on Iranian radar sites early on 6 June, following Tehran’s drone launches at US vessels, pushed a months-long escalation track into open regional confrontation that had been foreshadowed by Iran’s March warning that threats to its infrastructure would widen the conflict. By later that day, Iran had fired missiles at Bahrain and Kuwait, jolting Gulf states that were already balancing fragile security arrangements against fears of becoming battlegrounds, with immediate risks to civilian confidence, energy flows, and regional labor populations. In the occupied West Bank, Israeli troops’ killing of a seven-month-old Palestinian baby in Hebron after firing on a family vehicle underscored a separate but politically resonant front in which daily military force deepens Palestinian vulnerability and hardens wider regional anger. The combined picture is of a region where state-to-state escalation and intimate civilian trauma are feeding the same instability, narrowing space for de-escalation.
